mismatch.message: simple monster action requires a special monster action

summary: At zero-based step 34, JavaScript rejects the visible sleeping leprechaun in its simple-action preflight before reaching the source-supported wake check. C enters monmove.c:dochug() and calls disturb(); its hard-to-wake leprechaun gate draws rn2(50)=27 and returns 0, so the monster remains asleep and does not attack or steal gold. This is a source-traced false refusal in the JS action boundary, not an AD_SGLD/stealgold mismatch.

source.branch: A newly created hostile leprechaun is asleep, visible and adjacent to a non-stealthy hero. In dochug(), a sleeping monster first calls disturb(); for a leprechaun, disturb() requires !rn2(50) before later wake conditions. The recorded 27 fails that gate, so dochug() returns before movement or attack. JavaScript instead rejects this visible sleeping leprechaun in assertSimpleActionState() before the existing disturb/dochug path.
callers: C caller path: mon.c:movemon_singlemon() (1320) calls monmove.c:dochugw(mtmp, TRUE); dochugw() calls monmove.c:dochug(), which consumes disturb() at monmove.c:727-731. JavaScript maps this through mon.js:movemon_singlemon() and the allmain.js:1178 adapter to unported_monster_actions.js:runSimpleMonsterAction() and monmove.js:dochug().

JavaScript preflight path: allmain.js:1249 calls preflightSimpleMonsterActions(); its cloned run reaches unported_monster_actions.js:assertSimpleActionState() via runSimpleMonsterAction() before monmove.js:dochug() can call disturb().
dependencies: makemon.c:makemon() S_LEPRECHAUN branch (1327-1328) establishes the asleep precondition; js/makemon_create.js mirrors it.
monmove.c:disturb() returns an int consumed by dochug(); js/monmove.js:disturb() already contains the matching leprechaun rn2(50) gate and is called from js/monmove.js:dochug().

evidence: The immutable v19 C recording challenges/cases/v19/leprechaun-steals-carried-gold-c62.session.json matches the capsule recordingSha256. Normalized segment 0 step 32 records “A leprechaun appears next to you”; step 34 is a period wait and its first RNG entry is rn2(50)=27 @ disturb(monmove.c:348). Steps 33-38 are six period waits; the C outcome records no attack or theft and $773 carried gold.

Upstream makemon.c:1327-1328 sets msleeping=1 in the S_LEPRECHAUN branch. Upstream monmove.c:327-358 short-circuits the hard-to-wake test through !rn2(50) before the generic !rn2(7) wake condition; monmove.c:727-731 returns immediately when a sleeping monster is not disturbed.

The current JavaScript stop matches unported_monster_actions.js:272-360: assertSimpleActionState() admits only an unseen sleeping leprechaun, then throws UnsupportedSimpleMonsterActionError("a special monster action") for this visible leprechaun. runSimpleMonsterAction() invokes that guard before monmove.js:dochug() reaches its existing sleeping/disturb branch at 2488-2493. monmove.js:2172-2204 implements the source wake gate, including leprechauns.

The capsule evaluation at challenges/evaluations/20261002180737-v19.json records the step-34 stop, 34/39 screens, 2848/2902 RNG calls, and the exact “simple monster action requires a special monster action” error. The C62 comparison receipt at /tmp/teleport-loop-worker-c-20260925/.cache/C62-logs/bounded/run-4d3bfR/receipt.json has SHA-256 f67b1bae469ea6d1e7487319ecfbcc4052df1a70ac81aa7de0c7b3e9b00662a3; capsule C62 comparison run-4d3bfR identifies monmove.c:disturb as the first C-only call. No replay was needed.

The C62 capsule crosswalk classifies the prepared theft target as a wake-target miss: no AD_SGLD/stealgold call occurs. Those attack/theft functions are not the source owner of this mismatch; the source-backed fix is to let a sleeping leprechaun reach the ordinary disturb early-return path, leaving any later successfully-woken special action at its own explicit boundary.

The inspected C and JavaScript source files are unchanged since the independently checkpointed C62 integration at 168d97a870934a4ec84e006d19cfc20ba3fca7ff; this finding is recorded at current main 8583a972f66a872a8ad73c888a24dd01075481f4.
